Relevant: the payments stop, so they differ between the alternatives.
Relevant: it is an opportunity cost, receivable only if the depot closes.
Not relevant: it spreads a past payment. What the racking would fetch is relevant.
Not relevant: they continue and are merely re-apportioned.
Relevant: a future payment arising only on closure.
Relevant: a future cost that arises only on closure.
Relevant: a benefit forgone under one alternative.

Closing saves the wages, the apportionment nothing, and gains 90,000 of rent, against 140,000 of redundancy, 60,000 of delivery and 400,000 of lost contribution. The two figures that most people put first — the 2,000,000 and the depreciation — belong in neither column.
